title: Court Canvas
text: This animation will help you prepare your croquet courts for tournament play. We begin with a leveled empty lawn. Standard tournament croquet requires a flat, low-cut grass surface measuring 28 x 35 yards.

title: Step 1: Marking Length Boundaries
text: The Long sides, West and East boundary lines are measured out giving the court a length of 32 metres or 35 yards.

title: Step 2: Marking Width Boundaries
text: The North and South boundary lines are measured, completing the rectangular boundary line perimeter. The width of the court is 25.6 metres or 28 yards. All corners are square

title: Step 3: Placing Hoop 1 (South-West)
text: Hoop 1 is placed at the South-West area. Spacing is exactly 6.4 metres or 7 yards from both the adjacent West and South inside boundary edges.

title: Step 4: Placing Hoop 2 (North-West)
text: Hoop 2 is set at the North-West area, 6.4 metres or 7 yards from both the adjacent North and West inside boundaries.

title: Step 5: Placing Hoop 3 (North-East)
text: Hoop 3 is positioned at the North-East area, also 6.4 metres or 7 yards from both the adjacent North and East inside boundaries.

title: Step 6: Placing Hoop 4 (South-East)
text: Hoop 4 is placed at the South-East area, and also 6.4 metres or 7 yards from both the East and South inside boundary edges.

title: Step 7: Placing the Central Peg
text: The Centre Peg is driven into the exact center of the lawn: exactly 12.8 metres or 42 feet" from West/East boundaries, and 16 metres or 52 feet 6" from North/South boundaries. This step is displayed in a top-down 2D camera view to verify its center alignment.

title: Step 8: Placing Hoop 5 (South Center)
text: Hoop 5 (South Center) is placed on the longitudinal center line of the court, positioned exactly 6.4 metres or 7 yards South of the centre peg spot, leaving exactly 9.6 metres or 31 feet 6" to the South boundary.

title: Step 9: Placing Hoop 6 (North Center)
text: Hoop 6 (North Center) is placed on the longitudinal center line of the court, positioned exactly 6.4 metres or 7 yards North of the centre peg spot, leaving exactly 9.6 metres or 31 feet 6" to the North boundary.

title: Step 10: Marking the Start Corner
text: A 1-yard (0.91 metre) radius quarter-circle is painted in white at the South-East corner (Corner 4) to mark the Starting Area.

title: Step 11: Marking the Penalty Semi-Circles
text: Two semi-circular penalty areas of 0.91 metre or 1 yard radius are painted, centered on the halfway points of the West and East boundary lines.

title: Step 12: Placing the Corner Flags
text: Four corner flags are placed at the boundarie corners to aid play. Corner 1 Flag near Blue Hoop (South-West) is Blue, Corner 2 (North-West) is Red, Corner 3 (North-East) is Black, and Corner 4 (the GC Start Corner South-East) is Yellow.

title: Step 13: Dressing Halfway Offside Pegs
text: Eight white boundary pegs (halfway offside pegs) are driven into the boundary lines to mark halfway points and offside lines. 4 of the pegs are placed on the center point of each boundary and the other 4 are placed at each North / South end 3.2 metres either side of the centre line and peg. The sideline pegs are located on the inside edge of the boundary line
